A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BannerAgency. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BannerRequest400 experiments, human preference and refinement studies, human–LLM rating correlations, and implementation costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measurements of canvas overflow in generated designs.

M1.justification: The agent architecture, background-generation loop, memory-assisted refinement, design variation and SVG/Figma implementations are retained. Appendix A.6 discloses prompts for the existing system without establishing a change to its procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain BannerRequest400, the size and style demonstrations, six-language examples, and the exemplar images used for FID. The overflow analysis examines the existing banner-generation task rather than introducing distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: DALL-E3, FLUX.1-schnell and OpenCOLE remain the baselines in the corresponding comparisons. The existing GPT-4o/Claude and SVG/Figma variants are also retained; relocated comparison examples preserve their comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds an element-level canvas-overflow evaluation covering 416 GPT-4o designs with 2,220 elements and 408 Claude-3.5 designs with 2,510 elements (Appendix A.4, Table 6). The previously reported benchmark settings and human-study protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a focused error analysis measuring how frequently generated elements extend beyond canvas boundaries. Existing background-removal comparisons, refinement analyses, design variations and style/language demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Human-study participant information, correlation coefficients, significance reporting, rating standard deviations and refinement error bars are unchanged. The new overflow table reports counts and percentages without introducing uncertainty estimates or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports overflow rates of 1.85% (41/2,220 elements) for GPT-4o and 1.04% (26/2,510) for Claude-3.5. Matched benchmark, preference, refinement, cost and general-design values are unchanged. Some illustrative style/language variants are omitted.

T1.justification: The memory-aware variation equation and formalized background-generation algorithm are retained. v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free multimodal banner generation, component-level editability, versatility and the BannerRequest400 benchmark.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the overflow results as supporting spatial reliability and emphasizes manual repair through editability. Its Limitations section newly identifies unsupported artistic text effects; several other limitations restate v1's future-work points.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds substantial agent-prompt documentation, including layout patterns, typography, spacing and contrast guidelines, Figma tool/template instructions, reviewer criteria and refinement instructions. v1 provided tool descriptions and code snippets without these prompts. Conversely, two detailed baseline-example prompts are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including MapCoder, ChatDev, VisualWebArena, MMedAgent and DesignLab. These broaden the supporting references while retaining the paper's positioning around training-free, editable design from multimodal inputs.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains closely matched. v2 makes local wording and cross-reference edits, adopts author–year citations, organizes the supplement as Appendix A.1–A.7, and separates Conclusion, Limitations and Ethics Statement.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: opening galleries are condensed into Figure 7, comparison rows move to the appendix, and style/language panels are reduced. Tables are reordered, an overflow table and colored prompt boxes are added, and typography and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: The new agent prompts improve implementation transparency, while the overflow analysis and explicit limitations provide useful additional scrutiny. Existing benchmark and human-study evidence is retained. Removing two baseline-example prompts reduces some reproducibility detail, but the added documentation and focused validation provide a modest net improvement.
